title: APS 01 – Algorithm complexity
description: Midterm 1 theory: counting operations, Big O / Ω / Θ, comparing algorithms, the RAM model.

questions.question: Which of these is an asymptotic bound of the function f(x) = x^2 + 3x + 4?
Big Omega (Ω) is:

options.text: Asymptotic upper bound: execution time in the worst case
Asymptotic lower bound: execution time in the best case
Both a lower and an upper bound on the execution time

questions.question: What does Θ (theta) notation describe?

options.text: The memory used by the algorithm
Both a lower and an upper bound on the execution time

questions.question: Which of the offered has the highest complexity / will run the slowest?
The complexity of algorithms is measured with:
What does the complexity of an algorithm NOT depend on?

options.text: The hardware: processor speed, amount of memory
The loops and recursive calls in the algorithm

questions.question: Imagine there are two solutions to a problem. The first solution has two consecutive recursive calls that use almost the original number of elements. The second solution traverses half the elements in a loop and then the other half in a reverse loop. Which solution is more efficient and why?

options.text: The first, because recursion is always more efficient than a loop
The second, because it solves the problem in linear time instead of exponential
The first, because it has exponential complexity unlike the second which has double linear complexity
The first, because it has logarithmic complexity unlike the second which has linear complexity

questions.question: Imagine there are two solutions to a problem. The first solution has a recursive call with the number of input elements reduced by one. The second solution has two nested loops over all elements. Which solution is more efficient and why?

options.text: The second, because it has quadratic complexity unlike the first which has exponential
The first, because it has logarithmic complexity unlike the second which has quadratic
The first, because it has linear complexity unlike the second which has quadratic
The second, because loops are always more efficient than recursion

questions.question: Imagine there are two solutions to a problem. The first solution has two consecutive recursive calls that halve the number of input elements. The second solution traverses half of the elements in a loop. Which solution is more efficient and why?

options.text: The second, because it solves the problem with only half the elements, while the first needlessly handles the elements twice
The first, because it has logarithmic complexity unlike the second which has linear
The first, because it has logarithmic complexity unlike the second which has half-linear
The first, because recursion is always more efficient than a loop

questions.question: T(n) is O(g(n)) if:

options.text: T(n) < c·g(n) for every n ≥ 0, for every constant c
there are positive constants c and n0 such that T(n) < c·g(n) for every n > n0
there are positive constants c and n0 such that T(n) > c·g(n) for every n > n0

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of the Random Access Machine (RAM) model?

options.text: Every simple operation (+, *, -, =, if, call) takes one time unit
Loops take as many time units as they have iterations
The execution time depends on the processor speed
